transcript: Birdie
Hi! I help businesses figure out exactly what they need from a chatbot. Before we start — what's your name?
Derek Fenn
Derek. Who's asking exactly, is this Callum's doing again
Birdie
Ha, no accusations here — just me, Birdie, here to help you get a chatbot sorted. Nice to meet you, Derek! So, tell me a bit about your business — what do you do, and what's it called?
Derek Fenn
Fenn & Son. Locks and key cutting mostly, bit of appliance repair on the side. Been going 34 years, my father started it. Why d'you need to know all this for a chatbot anyway
Birdie

Fair question! The more I know about how Fenn & Son actually runs, the better I can spec out a chatbot that fits — rather than some generic thing that misses the mark. Good on you for keeping it going 34 years, that's no small thing. So what's the main headache you're hoping a chatbot could help with — is it missed calls, repetitive questions, booking hassle, something else?
Derek Fenn

Suppose it'd be the same questions over and over. People texting asking how much for this, how much for that. Can't be doing with typing prices out to every stranger on the internet. Half the time I don't even know who's asking or what they actually need till I see the job.
Birdie

That makes total sense — answering the same 'how much for X' question all day is exhausting. When people text you these questions, is that on your regular mobile number, WhatsApp, Facebook, your website, or a mix of a few?
Derek Fenn

Mostly this WhatsApp thing. Some on the Facebook page Callum set up years back, I don't even look at that half the time. Website's there but I forget the password half the time, never touch it. Landline's still the best way honestly, people just don't ring anymore for some reason.
Birdie

Good to know — so WhatsApp's really the main battleground. Would you be able to share a few real WhatsApp chats or screenshots of typical customer questions? You can just drop them in the 'uploads' folder next to this program, or paste a few example messages right here if that's easier — seeing real examples helps me ask much sharper questions.
Derek Fenn

Not sending screenshots over the internet, no. Could be anyone looking at those. But I'll tell you what they ask - "how much to change a lock", "can you cut a key today", "how much to open a safe", "my toaster's broken can you fix it". Same stuff, over and over. That's it really.
Birdie
No problem at all, totally understandable. Let's go through those one at a time then — starting with locks: when someone asks 'how much to change a lock', what's the typical price range you'd quote?
Derek Fenn

Depends what lock. uPVC cylinder, from £45 fitted. Mortice lock, from £60. But I'm not typing that out as gospel to every text - depends what's actually on the door when I look at it. That's why I tell 'em come in or ring the shop.
Birdie
Got it — 'from' prices only, with a nudge to come in or call for the exact quote. Makes sense. Now what about key cutting — is there a standard price per key, or does that vary by key type too?
Derek Fenn
Varies. £4 to £8 depending what key it is. Simple Yale type one end, car keys and fancy ones another. Not doing exact quotes over text for that either, bring the key in and I'll look at it.
Birdie
Makes sense, keys can be trickier than they look. Now, safe opening — that one sounds like it could vary a lot. What's the ballpark range you usually quote for opening a safe?
Derek Fenn

Could be £80, could be £300. Depends on the safe, depends what's happened to it, depends if it's even openable without wrecking it. Not giving a number till I've seen it in person. That one especially - people need to just ring or bring photos in... no wait, don't send me photos either. Just come to the shop.
Birdie

Understood — safes are a proper 'come in only' job, no photos even. Last one on pricing: the appliance repair side, like the toaster example — how do you usually handle those enquiries and what's the rough cost?
Derek Fenn

Flat £15 just to look at it, diagnostic fee. Toaster, kettle, iron, whatever. Repair on top of that depends what's wrong with it - sometimes not worth fixing, I tell 'em straight. That £15 stands whether I fix it or not, covers my time looking.
Birdie
Got it, flat £15 look-fee no matter what — fair enough. Now let's talk hours: what days and times is the shop open, and does that match when you're happy to take enquiries?
Derek Fenn

Shop's Monday to Friday half eight to five. Saturday nine to one. Shut Sunday, always have been. Sometimes I open late if I've had a job on the night before, can't help that.

As for enquiries - people can text whenever I suppose, doesn't mean I'll answer it quick. I'm not sat looking at the phone all day, got a shop to run.
Birdie
That's helpful, thanks. Is it just you running things day to day, Derek, or do you have anyone else — family, staff — helping out in the shop or on jobs?
Derek Fenn

Just me mostly. Got Callum, part-time lad, does deliveries and answers the phone sometimes but he don't know pricing proper so don't ask him for quotes. No "Son" in the name works there anymore before you ask, that's a long story. Why's this matter for a chatbot anyway
Birdie

Fair enough, no need to dig into that! It matters because if the chatbot ever needs to hand a tricky question to a real person, I need to know who's actually able to answer it — sounds like that's you and you alone for pricing. Now, thinking about what you actually want this chatbot to do day-to-day — are you picturing something simple, like it just answers the common questions and tells people your ranges and to come in/call, or would you want it to also handle actual bookings and take payments?
Derek Fenn

Not taking payments, no chance. Someone types their card into a box on my website, first I hear of it is when it's all gone wrong. Not doing bookings either really - can't have a machine promising Callum's dad'll be somewhere at 3 o'clock when I've got three jobs on already.

Just answering the same questions, giving the "from" prices, telling 'em to ring or come in for the real answer. That's all I want it doing. Keep it simple.
Birdie

Crystal clear — simple info bot only, no payments, no booking promises. One important one for a locksmith: if someone messages saying they're locked out right now or it's an emergency, how do you want the bot to handle that — point them to call the landline straight away, or something else?
Derek Fenn

Straight to the landline, every time. Don't want no bot telling someone locked out at midnight to "wait for a reply" - that's how you lose a customer and get a bad name. Emergency thing, phone rings, I answer or I don't, but at least they've tried the right way. And tell 'em straight - I don't much fancy being called after dark, but if it's before ten I'll usually pick up.
Birdie

Got it — landline for emergencies, always, no exceptions, but you'd rather not be rung much after dark. Roughly how many of these enquiry messages are you getting a week across WhatsApp and Facebook combined — a handful, a dozen, more?
Derek Fenn

Dunno exactly, never counted. Handful most days I'd say, maybe more Mondays after the weekend. Callum could probably tell you better, he looks at that Facebook thing more than I do. Why's the number matter anyway
Birdie

Fair, just a ballpark helps me judge how much the bot needs to handle at once — sounds like it's manageable either way. Last couple of things: what would actually make this chatbot a win in your eyes — fewer repeat texts to answer yourself, more people just turning up informed, something else?
Derek Fenn

Mostly the first thing - not having to type "come in or ring the shop" fifty times a week to people I don't know from Adam. If it does that and people stop asking me the same three questions over and over, that's a win far as I'm concerned. Don't need it doing anything clever. Just that.
Birdie
Perfect, that's a clear and sensible goal. Last practical question: do you have a rough budget or timeline in mind for getting this built, or are you still figuring that part out?
Derek Fenn

Still figuring that out, aren't I. Not paying some fortune for a machine that just repeats what I already told you. Whatever's cheapest and simplest, does that job and no more. Timeline - no rush, been doing it the old way 34 years, another few weeks won't kill me.
Birdie

Right, Derek, let me read back what I've got so you can check I've got it straight:

- Fenn & Son — locksmith and key cutting, plus appliance repairs, family-run for 34 years, just you plus Callum part-time (deliveries, sometimes phone, not pricing).
- Main channel is WhatsApp, some Facebook, website barely used, landline still works.
- Problem: too many repeat 'how much for X' texts from strangers, wasting your time.
- Prices: lock change from £45 (uPVC) / £60 (mortice); keys £4–£8 depending on type; safe opening £80–£300 (never quoted without seeing it, no photos); appliance diagnostic flat £15 regardless of outcome.
- Policy: no exact quotes over text for anything — bot should give 'from' prices only and tell people to call or come into the shop.
- Hours: Mon–Fri 8:30–5, Sat 9–1, closed Sunday, sometimes opens late.
- Emergencies/lockouts: always tell them to ring the landline immediately, never 'wait for a reply' — though you'd rather not get calls late at night.
- Scope: a simple FAQ/info bot only — no bookings, no payments, no appointment promises.
- Success = it stops you typing 'come in or ring the shop' fifty times a week.
- Budget: undecided, wants cheapest/simplest option. Timeline: no rush.
- Open items to follow up: exact enquiry volume (maybe check with Callum), and firming up a budget once you've seen some options.

Does all that look right, or is there anything you'd want to change?
Derek Fenn

Aye, that's about right. Though don't go calling it "family-run" - it's just me. Told you, no Son actually works here, that's just the name on the sign. Rest of it's fine I suppose.

Now you're not going to make me sit here typing all day are you, get on with sorting the thing out.
Birdie

Sorted, Derek — thanks for bearing with all the questions. I've got everything I need. We'll put together a simple info bot for WhatsApp that answers the common pricing questions with your 'from' ranges, always points people to call or come in for a firm quote, sends emergencies/lockouts straight to your landline, and doesn't touch bookings or payments. We'll follow up once we've nailed down a budget option for you. Cheers for your time — talk soon.

brief.business_description: Started by Derek's father 34 years ago; 'Son' is just the name on the sign — no son actually works there. Derek runs it solo, with Callum part-time helping with deliveries and sometimes answering the phone (but not pricing/quotes).
brief.problem_to_solve: Getting repetitive price-check texts/messages from strangers online without knowing who they are or what job they actually need until he sees it in person.
brief.conversation_volume: Rough estimate: a handful of enquiries most days, more on Mondays after the weekend. Derek isn't sure of exact numbers — suggests Callum may know better since he checks Facebook more.
brief.success_criteria: Success = the bot handles the repeated 'come in or ring the shop' responses so Derek doesn't have to type them out dozens of times a week to strangers. Wants it simple, nothing clever.
brief.budget: Not yet decided — wants 'whatever's cheapest and simplest' that does the job and no more.
brief.timeline: No rush — a few weeks is fine, no pressure.
services_and_pricing: Lock change - uPVC cylinder: from £45 fitted (final price depends on what's actually on the door)
Lock change - mortice lock: from £60 fitted (final price depends on what's actually on the door)
Key cutting: £4 to £8 depending on key type (simple Yale-type vs car keys/fancy ones) - no exact quote over text, bring key in
Safe opening: £80 to £300, highly variable depending on safe type/condition/whether it can be opened without damage - no quote given until seen in person

Appliance repair (toaster, kettle, iron, etc): flat £15 diagnostic/look fee charged regardless of outcome, repair cost on top depends on what's wrong (sometimes not worth fixing, Derek tells customer straight)
faq_answers: Common customer questions: 'how much to change a lock', 'can you cut a key today', 'how much to open a safe', 'my toaster's broken can you fix it'
business_policies: Appliance repair: flat £15 diagnostic fee applies whether or not the item is fixed, covers Derek's time to look at it.
Shop hours: Monday-Friday 8:30am-5pm, Saturday 9am-1pm, closed Sunday. Occasionally opens late if he had a night job before.
No online payments wanted — Derek is wary of card details being taken via the site/bot.
No bookings/appointment promises wanted — Derek doesn't want the bot committing him to a specific time since his schedule is unpredictable (multiple jobs at once).
escalation_rules: Derek doesn't want firm lock prices quoted as gospel over text — he prefers to tell customers to come in or ring the shop so he can see the actual lock/door first before confirming a price.
Key cutting prices also not quoted exactly over text — customer needs to bring the key in for Derek to look at it.
Safe opening: no price given over text/phone at all — Derek insists customers come to the shop in person; explicitly does NOT want photos sent either.
Callum (part-time staff) should not be asked for pricing/quotes as he doesn't know pricing properly — only Derek handles that.

Emergencies/lockouts: bot must never tell someone to 'wait for a reply' — always direct them to call the landline immediately. Derek says he'll usually pick up before 10pm but doesn't like being called after dark/late at night.
open_items: Exact enquiry volume unconfirmed — Derek estimates 'a handful most days, more on Mondays' but suggests Callum may have better numbers from Facebook.
Budget not yet decided — Derek wants 'cheapest and simplest' option but no figure given.
additional_notes: Derek declined to share screenshots/chat exports for privacy reasons; provided example questions verbally instead.
Customers can text any time, but Derek doesn't respond quickly — he's busy running the shop, not watching his phone.
